summary: Poolside AI, a newly emerging open-source lab, released Laguna XS.2, a 33-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with three billion active parameters, trained on Poolside's own infrastructure. The model is designed for agentic coding and long-horizon workflows and is licensed under Apache 2.0.

research.notes: Feature described in transcript; no formal release post cited.

summary: Kimi K2.6 ships with four specialised modes inside the Kimi chatbot: Instant for quick responses, Thinking for deep research, Agent for specialised tools such as slides, websites and stocks, and Agent Swarms which deploys multiple agents in parallel for long-horizon tasks. The Kimi CLI, OpenRouter and Kilo Code are listed as integration paths.

research.notes: Mode set is described in transcript and demonstrated in walkthrough.

summary: Internal Codex routing logs reference a GPT-5.6 rollout entry, and a separate model slug for a GPT-5.5 Codex variant was discovered in OpenAI backend logs. Both suggest dedicated coding and successor models are being prepared within weeks.

summary: Claude Code received a quality-of-life update including push notifications when long tasks finish or input is needed, a /res-style feature reportedly up to 67 percent faster on 40+ MB transcripts, a fix for the recurring re-login prompt, lower memory usage on Linux, concurrent MCP server connection on startup, and various paste, scroll and resize improvements.

title: Codebuff switches default routing to GLM 5.1

research.notes: Benchmark figures (68% to 83%) are first-party Codebuff numbers reported in the video; not independently verified.

title: Freebuff: free ad-supported AI coding agent built on Codebuff
summary: Freebuff is a zero-config, fully free AI coding CLI built on top of the open-source Codebuff platform. It is monetised through in-terminal ads rather than subscriptions and ships with nine built-in sub-agents (file picker, code reviewer, browser use, thinker, etc.). Output runs on a custom GPU deployment that delivers up to 300 tokens per second.

research.notes: Distributed via npm. Built on the Codebuff multi-agent architecture; free tier supported by ads displayed in the CLI.

title: Xiaomi releases MiMo v2.5 base native-omni model
summary: Alongside MiMo v2.5 Pro, Xiaomi has released MiMo v2.5, the base model in the family, as a native omni model with multimodal understanding and integrated agent capabilities. Both models ship under the MIT license.

research.notes: Native omni model; multimodal understanding plus agent capabilities. MIT license.

title: Lightpanda headless browser integrated into Hermes Agent
summary: Hermes Agent now integrates Lightpanda, an open-source headless browser engineered for AI and automation workloads, as a default browser backend with automatic Chrome fallback. The integration improves browser automation reliability for autonomous web tasks in Hermes.

research.description: Lightpanda: the headless browser designed for AI and automation

title: Hermes Agent adds background computer use on macOS
summary: NousResearch's Hermes Agent has shipped an early-preview background computer-use feature powered by KUA, allowing the agent to operate apps via mouse, keyboard and screen on macOS without taking over the user's active session. The integration works with any vision-capable model (Claude, GPT, Gemini, local VLMs); Windows and Linux support is planned.

research.description: The agent that grows with you
research.notes: Background computer-use is an early preview feature, macOS-only at launch, powered by KUA. Works with any vision-capable LLM.

title: Xiaomi open-sources MiMo v2.5 Pro trillion-parameter MoE
summary: Xiaomi has released MiMo v2.5 Pro, a roughly 1.02-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 42 billion active parameters, a 1 million token context window and hybrid attention. Released under the MIT license for commercial deployment, the model targets long-horizon agentic workflows and software engineering, reporting competitive scores on SWE-bench Pro, GDP-Eval and Claw-Eval versus Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.4 while using 40-60% fewer tokens. API pricing is $1 per million input tokens and $3 per million output tokens.

research.notes: MIT license. ~1.02T parameters / 42B active; trained FP8 across ~27T tokens. Sustains 1000+ tool calls. Released alongside the MiMo v2.5 base model (native omni). Available via MiMo Studio, OpenRouter and Kilo Code (with $25 free credits).

summary: Codebuff is the open-source terminal coding agent that powers Freebuff. It coordinates specialised sub-agents around a project rather than relying on a single model, and reportedly scored 61% versus Claude Code's 53% on a 175-task internal evaluation.

title: TinyFish makes Web Search and Fetch APIs free for all developers
summary: TinyFish has made its Web Search and Web Fetch APIs free for every developer and agent, with no credit card required. Search returns structured data with sub-500 ms latency; the Browser API spins up stealth Chrome sessions in under 250 ms; an Agent API handles multi-step tasks. Free-tier limits are 5 search queries per minute and 25 fetch URLs per minute.

research.notes: REST API, MCP server, Python/TypeScript SDKs, CLI; integrations with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, n8n, LangChain, CrewAI.

title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite heading to general availability on Vertex AI
summary: Google has emailed Vertex AI customers still on Gemini Flash 2 announcing the imminent general availability of Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, Google's most cost-effective model. Pricing is $0.25 per million input tokens and $1.50 per million output tokens, with an Arena Elo of 1432 reported at launch.

research.notes: Pricing $0.25 / $1.50 per 1M input/output tokens. Available via Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Vertex AI.

title: Hermes Agent ships Kanban board for multi-agent orchestration
summary: Hermes Agent has updated its built-in Kanban to support unlimited boards and projects, with subscriptions to project updates routed through the Nous Tool Gateway messenger. The board provides a workspace for orchestrating multiple agents across to-do, in-progress and done states, complementing the new /goal command for long-running autonomous objectives.

research.notes: Kanban initialised via 'hermes kanban' commands; pairs with /goal command for autonomous objective mode similar to Codex and Claude Code.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 4.7
summary: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 4.7, its most capable Opus model. SWE-bench Verified rises from 80.8% to 87.6% versus Opus 4.6 and SWE-bench Pro from 53.4% to 64.3%; MCP-Atlas reaches 77.3%, a leading score for multi-tool orchestration. Vision processes images at over three times higher resolution. Pricing is unchanged at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens. Anthropic warns that prompts tuned for Opus 4.6 may need retuning because the new model interprets instructions more literally.

research.notes: Released 2026-04-16. Available on Claude Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, the API, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry. First Claude model to pass Anthropic's 'implicit-need' tests. Reasoning tiers shifted up one notch (low ~ old medium, etc.). Token usage per task is higher than Opus 4.6.

title: Traycer launches Bart Mode for autonomous epic execution
summary: Traycer has launched Bart Mode, an outer-loop AI orchestrator that takes an epic, breaks it into tickets and runs them as parallel agent batches, reviewing each batch against the spec and updating the plan when new information emerges. The mode is agent-agnostic and orchestrates whichever coding agent is connected (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Kilo Code). A complementary team-collaboration feature has also been rolled out.

research.notes: Bart Mode (internally 'Smart YOLO') manages a feedback loop across specs, tickets, diffs and verification results. Distinct from Ralph-style retry loops. Available via the Traycer IDE extension for Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf.

title: Claude Jupiter codename surfaces ahead of Anthropic dev event
summary: Strings referencing an internal Anthropic model codenamed 'Claude Jupiter version 1' were discovered, reportedly undergoing red-teaming, jailbreak testing and constitutional-classifier evaluation under Anthropic's responsible scaling policy. Speculation links it to a Sonnet 4.8 or Haiku 4.7 release at the Code with Claude conference on May 6.

research.notes: Codename leak reported by testing-catalog; not officially confirmed by Anthropic.

title: Moonshot Kimi K2.6: open-source coding model with agent swarms
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi Chat 2.6 (Kimi K2.6), an open-source 1T-parameter coding model reporting state-of-the-art results on SWE-bench, BrowserComp and advanced math and vision tasks. Features include 12+ hour coding sessions, 4,000+ tool calls, 300 parallel agent swarms, multi-language multi-file generation, and pricing roughly 94% and 95% cheaper than Opus 4.6 on input and output respectively. Runs locally via MLX on dual M3 Ultra Macs.

research.description: Kimi K2 is the large language model series developed by Moonshot AI team
research.notes: K2.6 builds on the Kimi K2 series; weights released under a Modified MIT license per Moonshot's repository.

title: DeepSeek V4 rumored as 1.6T-parameter MoE
summary: Reports attributed to a Princeton AI Lab fellow describe DeepSeek V4 as a 1.6T-parameter MoE model with sparse MQA, fused MoE kernels and hyperconnections, with leaked figures around 99.4% MMLU and 83.7% SWE-bench. Requires roughly a 512 GB-class machine to run locally even quantized.

research.notes: Unverified leak; benchmark numbers not independently confirmed.

title: OpenAI Codex 'pets' overlay and migration importer
summary: OpenAI added a /pet and /hatch command set to Codex that spawns an animated desktop companion showing live agent status (active thread, running, waiting, ready for review). A separate migration system imports settings, plugins, agents and project configurations from other tools into Codex.

research.notes: Feature described in transcript; verify in official OpenAI Codex changelog.

title: Claude Code silent prompt compaction update
summary: Claude Code revised its system-prompt compaction: trimming is now silent (no explicit alerts) and the compaction prompt is tuned to better preserve sensitive instructions and original user intent during long-running sessions.

research.notes: Behaviour change described in transcript; specific release notes not located.

title: GitHub Copilot Max tier appears at $99/month
summary: A new GitHub Copilot Max subscription tier was spotted as a placeholder, priced at $99 per month, positioned as a higher-end plan aimed at power users and advanced AI workflows as part of a broader Copilot lineup revamp.

research.notes: Pre-launch placeholder; pricing and feature set may change before GA.

title: Google tests new Gemini checkpoints and Colab-style agent
summary: Newer Gemini checkpoints, possibly labelled Gemini 3.2 Pro or 3.5 Pro, are being A/B tested inside Google AI Studio ahead of Google I/O. A separate Colab-style competitor inside Gemini, currently referred to as 'agent', is reported, expected to automate Google Workspace tasks. Google has also extended subscription access inside AI Studio, raising coding limits and exposing pro models without an API key.

research.notes: Pre-I/O speculation; version labels and product framing not officially confirmed.

title: Qwen 3.6 Max Preview: Alibaba's flagship agentic coding model
summary: Alibaba released Qwen 3.6 Max Preview, a flagship preview model built on Qwen 3.6 Plus with stronger world knowledge, instruction following and agentic coding. It targets multi-step development workflows, front-end generation, visual reasoning, and browser-based visual agent tasks with a 1M token context window. Priced at $1.30 per 1M input tokens and $7.80 per 1M output tokens.

research.notes: Preview accessible via Alibaba's chatbot and API; not available through OpenRouter or Kilo at time of recording. Reported to outperform Claude 4.5 Opus and GLM 5.1 on selected benchmarks per the transcript.

title: Claude managed agents: multi-agent orchestration and webhooks
summary: Anthropic expanded Claude managed agents with multi-agent orchestration (lead agent delegating to parallel specialists), an outcome-loop self-evaluation system against predefined rubrics, a dreaming capability for reviewing past sessions, and webhook support for external integration.

research.notes: Capabilities described from conference talk; verify against Anthropic's official release notes when available.

title: GPT 5.5 'Spud' reportedly in A/B testing inside ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI's next mid-cycle model, referred to as GPT 5.5 and codenamed 'Spud', is reported to be A/B tested inside ChatGPT. Early demos highlight gains in speed, token efficiency, reasoning, SVG and 3D generation, and front-end coding. Polymarket positioning suggests imminent release.

research.notes: Pre-release A/B leak; model name and timing not confirmed by OpenAI.

title: Claude Cardinal: in-app memory and usage analytics dashboard

research.notes: Unreleased feature observed in app strings; not officially announced.

title: Anthropic roadmap: infinite context and long-horizon reasoning

research.notes: Forward-looking roadmap statements. The 'Mythos architecture' and 'Claude 5' framing is speculative.

title: Arc-AGI 3 benchmark scores released for frontier models

research.notes: Specific score values from transcript; check arcprize.org leaderboard for canonical numbers.

research.notes: Launched 5 May 2026 with a $29M seed round. Claims benchmark scores of 95.0 on RULER-128K, 65.9 on MRCR v2 at 1M tokens, 81.8 on SWE-Bench Verified. Independent verification has been requested by researchers.

title: Shai-Hulud npm worm compromises 169 packages
summary: A self-propagating supply-chain worm slipped through npm Trusted Publishing by abusing GitHub Actions pull_request_target on TanStack, then spread via stolen tokens to packages at Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenSearch, and Guardrails AI; security firm Aikido tracked 373 poisoned versions across 169 packages.

research.notes: Compromised packages carry valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance attestations — the first npm worm documented to produce validly-attested malicious packages. Attacker pwned a fork-triggered pull_request_target workflow, then extracted OIDC tokens from /proc/<pid>/mem of the GitHub Actions runner.

web_findings.title: Mini Shai-Hulud Worm Compromises TanStack, Mistral AI, Guardrails AI & More Packages
web_findings.snippet: 84 npm artifacts across 42 @tanstack/* packages compromised on May 11 2026 by chaining GitHub Actions Pwn Request, cache poisoning and OIDC token exploitation.

title: Kernel open-sources GPU-accelerated browser sandbox for agents
summary: Kernel provides open-source browser infrastructure that spins up sandboxed Chromium instances in under 30 ms on GPU-accelerated hardware, aimed at AI agent workloads. Includes session replay for debugging; in production at Framer and Cash App, billed only when active.

research.notes: Founded 2025 by Rafael Garcia and Catherine Jue (YC). Unikernel-per-browser architecture; reports <325 ms cold start vs 3–5 s for container-based equivalents.

web_findings.title: Kernel: Browser infrastructure for web agents and automations
web_findings.snippet: Sandboxed unikernel per browser; MP4 replay; Apache-2.0 infra and SDKs.

web_findings.title: kernel/kernel-images — GitHub
web_findings.snippet: Browsers-as-a-service for automations and web agents.

web_findings.title: Kernel vs Browserbase — Kernel Blog
web_findings.snippet: Reports 5.8× faster cold starts and 50–98% lower cost vs Browserbase.

title: Hermes Agent: autonomous framework for tool-using AI agents
summary: Framework from Nous Research that combines language models with memory, APIs, file operations, and iterative execution loops to drive multi-step autonomous workflows.

research.notes: Nous Research's flagship self-evolving agent. Companion repos exist for plugins, function-calling, self-evolution and compression evaluation.

title: Telegraf: plugin-driven metrics collection agent
summary: InfluxData's open-source agent for collecting metrics, logs, and events through a large plugin ecosystem, forwarding to time-series databases and observability platforms.

title: Sentry ships Seer agent for production debugging
summary: Sentry launched Seer, an AI agent that investigates production errors by pulling traces, spans, logs, and replays from existing Sentry data, walking upstream across services to identify root cause, and drafting fixes as pull requests. Open beta.

research.notes: Seer Agent launched April 28 2026; January 2026 update added local-development and code-review debugging plus flat unlimited pricing.

web_findings.title: Sentry Launches Seer Agent — Sentry press release
web_findings.snippet: Investigate production problems in plain language; multi-player from Slack.

web_findings.title: Sentry's Seer Agent lets developers debug production issues in natural language — The New Stack
web_findings.snippet: Walks the dependency graph across services to identify root cause and draft fixes.

web_findings.title: Sentry Expands Seer AI Debugging Agent to Local Development and Code Review
web_findings.snippet: PR-level defect analysis and background root-cause triage on incoming errors.

title: ds4: compact systems-programming data structures in C (antirez)
summary: Antonio (antirez) Sanfilippo's compact C library of efficient data structures for systems programming; targets memory and runtime efficiency in low-level applications.

research.notes: The video summary mis-identifies the project: antirez/ds4 is in fact a local inference engine for DeepSeek 4 Flash (Metal and CUDA), not a generic data-structures library. Worth tracking on the strength of the author and the topic.

title: Hermes proxy: route one subscription across coding agents
summary: A local OpenAI-compatible proxy in Hermes 0.14 lets a single Claude/ChatGPT/Grok subscription drive any compatible coding agent without separate API keys — runs as a local host endpoint authenticated by the user's existing plan.

research.notes: Ships as part of Hermes Agent 0.14 — exposes a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint backed by the user's chat subscription.

title: OpenSRE: AI-assisted platform for SRE workflows
summary: Open-source SRE platform combining observability, diagnostics, and operational tooling with AI assistance for incident response and reliability automation.

title: Awesome AI Agents: curated directory of agent frameworks
summary: Curated index of AI-agent frameworks, multi-agent systems, orchestration tools, and autonomous-workflow projects — a discovery hub for comparing approaches.

title: Hysteria: high-performance proxy and tunneling protocol
summary: Open-source proxy and tunneling system using modern transport protocols to improve latency and throughput across unstable or restricted networks.

title: MTEB: benchmark suite for embedding models
summary: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark — datasets, evaluation pipelines, and standardised metrics for comparing retrieval, classification, and semantic similarity across embedding models.

research.notes: Video calls this 'MTV'; the canonical project is MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark).

title: pnpm 11 ships supply-chain mitigations by default
summary: pnpm 11 enables three defaults that block this class of attack: minimumReleaseAge refuses packages younger than 24 hours, blockExoticSubdependencies refuses non-registry transitive deps, and approvedBuilds disables install scripts unless whitelisted.

web_findings.title: pnpm — Fast, disk space efficient package manager
web_findings.snippet: minimumReleaseAge, blockExoticSubdependencies and approved-builds are documented as defaults from v11.
